claims.text: The new errors field in the POST /users response is a hash keyed by field name, which has the same name but a different shape than the existing errors (a string array) used elsewhere in the same controller.
There is no test coverage for the new errors/values response fields added to UsersController that the frontend depends on.
There is no test coverage for EmailValidator's short-circuit branch that skips should_block? when the email already has other validation errors.
Email.downcase() only lowercases the domain part, not the local part, so using it won't fix the case-sensitivity issue - need to use full downcase instead
Case-sensitive email lookup in BlockedEmail.should_block? creates bypass risk - User@Example.com can bypass a block on user@example.com
Should a blocked registration attempt reveal to the requester that the specific email address is on the block list, since the current response allows enumerating the list?
The new EmailValidator file is missing a trailing newline at end of file.

pushObject(result.values.email) will add null/undefined if the server response omits values.email or returns it blank, leaving a non-string entry in rejectedEmails - should ensure value is present before caching
Potential duplicate entries in rejectedEmails array if user submits same blocked email multiple times
No updated specs for the changes to UsersController#create

BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
Consider using the new user.email.blocked translation key instead of user.email.invalid for blocked email validation messages
Extra blank lines at start/end of describe block in email_validator_spec.rb violate RuboCop Layout/EmptyLinesAroundBlockBody convention
should_block? returns nil instead of false when no matching record exists, violating the predicate-method (?) convention of always returning a boolean.
rejectedEmails is declared in the class body, so the Ember.A([]) array actually lives on the prototype and is shared across all controller instances.
BlockedEmail.should_block? should use email.downcase when querying to ensure case-insensitive matching
email_validator.rb file is missing a trailing newline
Normalize the email before querying in BlockedEmail.should_block?; otherwise blocked addresses can be bypassed by changing case

Em.A([]) defined directly on the class body creates a shared mutable array across all instances of CreateAccountController, causing rejected emails from one instance to bleed into every other instance - should be initialized in init hook instead
Missing regression test covering nil/blank value when whitelist/blacklist settings are present to ensure validation doesn't raise unexpectedly

email_in_restriction_setting? calls value =~ regexp which will raise if value is nil (e.g., missing email param) even though presence validation would already fail - need to guard validate_each / email_in_restriction_setting? against blank/nil values
UsersController#create now returns user.errors.to_hash which could potentially leak internal validation details

Rejected email cached with server-normalised casing causes case-sensitivity mismatch - server stores downcased email but client checks rejectedEmails.contains(email) against raw input, allowing users to bypass client-side guard by retyping with different casing
The new EmailValidator uses the `and` keyword instead of `&&` in a conditional, which is a low-precedence pitfall.
Regex pattern @(#{domains}) only matches domain suffixes, not full domains. evil.example.com would match whitelist entry example.com.
BlockedEmail model needs email normalization via before_validation callback to downcase emails before storage
Missing newline at end of file which will cause noisy diffs and may trigger linter warnings
The field-level error message shown for a blocked email is a generic "invalid", inconsistent with the specific server message shown in the flash.
How will the blocked_emails table actually be populated, given there is no admin UI, rake task, or seed data to insert records?
The blocked-email lookup does a case-sensitive string comparison, so changing the case of one letter in a blocked address bypasses the block entirely.
EmailValidator no longer rejects malformed email addresses, so validates :email, email: true can now accept values like sam@sam or sam

The computed property depends on rejectedEmails.@each but @each is mainly for observing per-item properties and can be unreliable for array membership changes with primitive items like strings - may not recompute when pushObject is called depending on Ember version
set_defaults is declared as a public instance method even though it is only meant to be used as an internal before_validation callback.
The new BlockedEmail model name collides conceptually with the existing User#blocked concept (suspended accounts), which refers to something different.
The return value of record.save when updating match_count is discarded, so if the save ever fails validation, the stats silently stop updating with no signal.
No updated specs for the modified User model validations
